prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: A fairer, greener UK that tackles the cost-of-living, rebuilds public services, and addresses the climate and nature emergencies together. Funded by taxing wealth and pollution, public ownership of key utilities, and major green investment.

Health and social care
- NHS: Restore a fully public service; more GP and dentist access; fair pay to retain staff; reduce waiting lists. Extra NHS spending rising to £28bn/yr by 2030, plus £20bn capital over five years.
- Primary care/public health: +£1.5bn/yr for GPs by 2030; £2bn capital; restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn); expand community diagnostics.
- Dentistry: New NHS contract; investment to £3bn/yr by 2030.
- Mental health: Therapies within 28 days; tailored services; counsellor in every school/college.
- Assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; rebuild workforce with national pay/careers; invest £20bn/yr. Extra £3bn for children’s social care. Improve rights and benefits for disabled people and carers.

Homes and planning
- Build 150,000 social homes/yr; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no-fault evictions.
- Retrofit and resilience: £29bn home insulation (to EPC B), £9bn low‑carbon heat, £7bn heat adaptation, £4bn for public buildings; area-based local programmes.
- New builds: Passivhaus/equivalent; solar and heat pumps mandatory; protect green belt; require low-car access and whole-life carbon assessments.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas; end subsidies; rising carbon tax; wind ~70% of electricity by 2030 (targets: 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore); 100GW solar by 2035; remove barriers to community energy; expand grid, storage, interconnectors; green hydrogen for industry. End biomass imports/subsidies. Stop new nuclear; phase out existing.

Economy and tax
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr (clean power, homes, rail, water, industry, active travel).
- Public ownership of rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Tax reform: Wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align Capital Gains and investment income with earnings; reform inheritance/pension relief; remove NI upper limit; long‑term Land Value Tax; higher windfall taxes; VAT shifts (cut for hospitality/arts, raise for private education/financial services); carbon tax £120/t rising toward £500/t. Clamp down on avoidance.

Work and welfare
- Repeal anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage (support for SMEs); 10:1 pay ratios; full rights for gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Welfare: +£40/wk to UC/legacy; scrap 5‑week wait and two-child cap; +5% disability benefits; protect pensions; +10% carers’ allowance; end sanctions; long‑term Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% land/sea by 2030; rewet peat; boost woodlands/hedgerows; Right to Roam; bring water into public ownership; stronger Clean Air Act; +£1.5bn for DEFRA/EA/NE.
- Animal protection commission; ban blood sports, lead ammo, factory farming practices; end badger cull.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support for agroecology; cut pesticides; expand horticulture; free school meals for all and free breakfast clubs to Year 6; local food partnerships.

Education
- +£8bn for schools (+£2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr to fix buildings (RAAC); £5bn for SEND; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; bring academies under local control; VAT on private school fees (SEN exempt); restore grants and scrap tuition fees; £1.4bn/yr for Sure Start; extend childcare to 35 hrs from 9 months.

Transport
- Public transport: Subsidies to £10bn/yr; £19bn over five years for rail, buses, EV infrastructure, walking/cycling; rail back to public ownership; local control of buses; £2.5bn/yr for active travel; oppose new roads; road pricing; default 20mph in built‑up areas; ICE sales end by 2027, road use by 2035; EV scrappage up to £5bn/yr; aviation frequent‑flyer levy; ban short domestic flights where rail <3 hours; no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: Proportional representation; repeal voter ID; state party funding; tougher lobbying/media transparency; votes at 16; elected second chamber; defend ECHR/HRA; self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration: End hostile environment/NRPF; safe routes; right to work while claiming asylum; family reunion; simplify/at-cost visas; new Department of Migration.

Justice and drugs
- Rebuild trust in policing; end routine stop-and-search and facial recognition; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; invest to clear court backlogs; make misogyny a hate crime; decriminalise sex work; evidence-led drug reform and decriminalise personal possession.

Foreign policy
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; EU rejoin path (Customs Union, free movement, Erasmus).
- Israel–Palestine: Immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognise Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, pursue war crimes accountability.
- Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI; support Loss and Damage; debt relief; ecocide law.
- Sign TPNW; cancel Trident; work within NATO for reform and no-first-use.
